text:
Predicates:
WorksInStudentJobs(x) ::: x works in student jobs on campus.
OrdersTakeoutFrequently(x) ::: x orders takeout frequently in college.
EnjoysDiningHallMeals(x) ::: x enjoys the dining hall meals and recipes.
PickyEater(x) ::: x is a picky eater.
SpendsTimeEatingAndCatchingUp(x) ::: x spends a lot of their time eating and catching up with friends in the campus dining halls.
AtSchool(x) ::: x is at Mary's school.
Hannah(x) ::: x is Hannah.
Premises:
∀x (WorksInStudentJobs(x) → NeedsMoney(x)) ::: If people work in student jobs, then they need to earn money to help pay for college tuition.
∀x (OrdersTakeoutFrequently(x) → WorksInStudentJobs(x)) ::: If people order takeout frequently, then they work in student jobs.
∀x (OrdersTakeoutFrequently(x) ∨ (EnjoysDiningHallMeals(x) ∧ Recipes(x))) ::: People order takeout frequently or enjoy dining hall meals and recipes.
∀x (EnjoysDiningHallMeals(x) → ¬PickyEater(x)) ::: If people enjoy dining hall meals, then they are not picky eaters.
∀x (EnjoysDiningHallMeals(x) → SpendsTimeEatingAndCatchingUp(x)) ::: If people enjoy dining hall meals, they spend a lot of time eating and catching up.
Hannah ∧ WorksInStudentJobs(Hannah) ::: Hannah is at Mary's school and works in student jobs.
(NeedsMoney(Hannah) → (¬PickyEater(Hannah) ∧ NeedsMoney(Hannah))) ::: If Hannah needs to earn money, then she is neither a picky eater nor needs to earn money.
Conclusion:
AtSchool(Hannah) ∧ (¬PickyEater(Hannah) ∨ (PickyEater(Hannah) → SpendsTimeEatingAndCatchingUp(Hannah))) ::: Hannah is at Mary's school and she either is not a picky eater or, if she is, then she spends a lot of her time eating and catching up with friends in the campus dining halls.
